record.paper_title: Open Problems in Hydrodynamical Approach to Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
record.original_question: How should event-by-event fluctuations in the non-smooth initial energy configuration of high-energy nuclear collisions be incorporated into hydrodynamical calculations so that event-averaged observables, especially the elliptic-flow coefficient v2 that measures azimuthal flow anisotropy, can be predicted quantitatively and used to recover information about the early collision state?

evidence.quote: The finite positive value of this coefficient v2 is referred to as the elliptic flow and, from the point of view of hydrodynamics, it is sensitive to the initial pressure gradient of the system.

Even the mechanism of thermalization is fast enough, the initial condition attained by high energy nuclear collision event is far from smooth as shown by the event generators such as NeXUS code. Furthermore, this initial configuration fluctuates collision by collision very largely, even for central collision of heavy nuclei.

Since the dynamical evolution of hydrodynamics is extremely non-linear, the event average of any hydrodynamical obserbable is quite different from the value calculated from the averaged smooth initial configuration, which is the hydrodynamcal calculations commonly used. The fluctuation of v2 coefficient must contain the dynamical information of the state formed in the early stage of the collision.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the hydrodynamical modeling of high-energy heavy-ion collisions, in which a hot, dense medium produced shortly after the collision is treated as a relativistic fluid evolving from an initial energy/entropy density profile to freeze-out. Define the elliptic-flow coefficient v_2 as the second Fourier coefficient of the azimuthal distribution of produced particles,
  dN/dφ ∝ 1 + 2 Σ_{n≥1} v_n cos(n(φ − Ψ_n)),
so that v_2 = ⟨cos 2(φ − Ψ_2)⟩, where Ψ_2 is an event-plane angle. Because the colliding nuclei are composed of nucleons whose positions fluctuate event by event, the initial energy-density configuration is not smooth: it varies strongly from collision to collision, even at fixed impact parameter. Because relativistic hydrodynamic evolution is highly nonlinear, the event average of an observable computed from fluctuating initial conditions generally differs from the value obtained by evolving a single smooth (event-averaged) initial condition.

Develop a quantitative framework that:
(a) specifies how to sample/parametrize fluctuating, non-smooth initial energy-density configurations characteristic of high-energy nuclear collisions;
(b) evolves each such configuration through (viscous or ideal) relativistic hydrodynamics to compute v_2 and its event-by-event distribution;
(c) yields event-averaged observables, in particular ⟨v_2⟩ and the variance of v_2, that match experimental measurements as a function of centrality and transverse momentum; and
(d) allows the early-stage properties of the produced matter (e.g., initial geometry, pressure gradients, thermalization time, transport coefficients) to be inferred from these observables.

State and justify the precise prescription for incorporating event-by-event initial-state fluctuations into hydrodynamic calculations needed to achieve (a)–(d).
artifact.status_search_result: Since 2010–2011, event-by-event (viscous) hydrodynamics with Monte Carlo Glauber/KLN-type fluctuating initial conditions has become a standard tool. Such calculations reproduce the measured centrality and pT dependence of v_2 and predict higher harmonics (v_3, etc.) arising purely from fluctuations. Thus the qualitative prescription posed in 2006 is now well-developed and broadly successful, while quantitative extraction of early-stage properties (initial conditions, η/s, thermalization) remains an active area with model-dependent uncertainties — hence partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Event-by-event hydrodynamics and elliptic flow from fluctuating initial state
status_evidence.snippet: Framework for event-by-event ideal hydrodynamics with fluctuating MC-Glauber initial conditions reproduces centrality and pT dependence of v_2 at RHIC.
status_evidence.claim: Event-by-event hydrodynamics with fluctuating initial conditions reproduces measured v_2.

status_evidence.title: Elliptic and Triangular Flow in Event-by-Event Viscous Hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Viscous event-by-event hydrodynamics produces both v_2 and v_3 from initial-state fluctuations.
status_evidence.claim: Initial-state fluctuations in viscous hydrodynamics generate v_2 and v_3 consistent with data.

status_evidence.title: Eccentricity fluctuations in an integrated hybrid approach: Influence on elliptic flow
status_evidence.snippet: Eccentricity fluctuations are essential to reproduce centrality dependence of elliptic flow.
status_evidence.claim: Fluctuations must be included for quantitative v_2 predictions.
